Rashi on Eruvin 7a:10:1.english: He picked an etrog - All trees are called “etrog”.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:10:2.hebrew: שני עישורין - שניה יוצאה ושלישית נכנסת, הואי שנה שניה לשמיטה מעשר ראשון ושני והשלישית מעשר ראשון ומעשר עני:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:10:2.english: Two tithes - The second [tithe] departs and the third [tithe] enters: that is, in the second year of the sabbatical cycle, [one separates] first tithe and second tithe; and in the third [year], first tithe and poor-man's tithe.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:10:3.english: One, like the words of Beit Shammai - who say: on the first of Shevat is the New Year for trees, and [the tree] has already entered its third year:

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:10:4.english: And one [ruling is] in accordance with the words of Beit Hillel - who say: until the fifteenth of it [Shevat] it is not the New Year, and it is still the second [year].

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:11:1.english: His tradition left him in doubt - And in all of it he followed Beit Hillel:

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:12:1.english: Dispute - [concerning] open-ended alleys: [the position of] the Tanna Kamma and Chananya.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:12:2.hebrew: סרטיא ופלטיא - שתיהן רה"ר, כדאמרינן ביציאות השבת (שבת ד' ו.) איזהו רה"ר? סרטיא ופלטיא, סרטיא דרך הילוך בני אדם, פלטיא רחוב לשווקים, והיכא דשני ראשין מפולשין ברה"ר הוא דפליג חנניה ואמר בעי דלת:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:12:2.english: Sartia and Platia - Both are public domain, as we said in the chapter on the departures of Shabbat (Shabbat 4, 6.): "What is public domain? Sartia and Platia. Sartia is the path of human traffic; Platia is a street leading to the markets." Where both ends of an alleyway open onto the public domain, it is Hananiah who disagrees and says it requires a door:

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:13:1.english: A valley - It is a karmelit, and its prohibition is rabbinic.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:16:1.english: And he concludes with it - Rav Yosef, in the name of Rav Yehuda, [stated it] without attribution, and Rav Yehuda did not tell Rav Yosef from whom he received this conclusion. For if the end of this alleyway, the one open to the public domain, [opens] into a rechuvah, and the alleyway is open through the rechuvah because the wall of the rechuvah opposite it was breached to the public domain (*). A rechuvah is the enclosed courtyard behind houses, i.e., a rechuvah is an area surrounded by four partitions:

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:16:2.hebrew: אין צריך כלום - לתקן אותה פתיחה של צד הרחבה אלא ראש המופלש לרה"ר צריך לחי או קורה כתורת מבוי סתום ועל כרחיך בדנפרצה נמי רחבה כנגד פרצת המבוי בכותל שכנגדו לרה"ר אתא לאשמועינן ואמפולשין דלעיל קאי דאי ברחבה סתומה לגמרי פשיטא דהא סתימה מעלייתא היא והא ליכא למימר דמשום בני רחבה איצטריך לאשמועינן דלא אסרי אבני מבוי ואפילו לא עירבו עמהן, דהא נמי פשיטא דרחבה לא בעיא לערובי דסתם רחבה אין בה דיורין לצאת ולבא ואין תשמישה תדיר כדאמרינן בפרק שני (ד' כה.), מאן דשרי לטלטולי מן המבוי לתוכה משום דלית בה דיורין והלכתא כוותיה דקיימא לן בכל התורה רב אחא לחומרא ורבינא לקולא והלכתא כרבינא לקולא בר מאומצא ביעי ומזריקי, ורחבה לאו דוקא נקט והוא הדין לחצר שיש בה דיורין וערבו אלא עובדא ברחבה היתה כדאמרינן לקמן עובדא הוה בדורא דרעותא כו'. כל כניסה ויציאה דבתים שבהש"ס דרך החצר הוא וחצר לפני הבתים:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:16:2.english: There is no need for anything - It is not necessary to emend that opening of the side of the rehava. Rather, the open end that breaches into the public domain requires a lechi or a beam, following the law of a dead-end alley. And you must concede that even when a rehava is breached, it requires a lechi or beam opposite the breach of the alley, in the wall across from it that opens to the public domain. It comes to teach us that the 'breached' case mentioned above applies here. For if it were a completely enclosed rehava, it would be obvious, since it is a perfectly valid closure. Nor can one say that it was necessary to teach this for the sake of the residents of the rehava, namely that the residents of the alley do not prohibit carrying for them even if they did not join in an eruv with them. For that too is obvious: a rehava does not need an eruv, since an ordinary rehava has no residents going out and coming in, and its use is not constant, as we stated in the second chapter (page 25), regarding one who permits carrying from the alley into it because it has no residents. The halakha follows him, as we hold throughout the Torah: Rav Acha is stringent and Ravina is lenient, and the halakha follows Ravina for leniency, except for ma'umtza, eggs, and mezarikei. The term rehava was not used precisely; the same applies to a courtyard that has residents and whose residents joined an eruv. Rather, the case occurred in a rehava, as we say below: 'the incident occurred in Dura de-Ra'uta.' Every entrance and exit of houses mentioned in the Talmud is through the courtyard, and the courtyard lies in front of the houses.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:17:1.hebrew: הא דר"י - הא דסיימת משמיה דרב יהודה, ולא פירש לך ממאן גמרה, כדמפרש ברישא דמילתיה משמיה דרב, האי סיומא ע"כ, משמואל רביה גמרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:17:1.english: That which R. Yehuda [said] - That which you concluded in the name of Rav Yehuda and did not tell us from whom he learned it, as it explains at the beginning of his statement, [that it is] in the name of Rav, this conclusion he must necessarily have learned from Shmuel, his teacher.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:1:1.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua - [His view is stated] in the chapter Hazahav in Bava Metzia (59b):

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:2:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - הרוצה לעשות דקתני, לאו בית שמאי ובית הלל דווקא נקט, על כרחיך כב"ה בעי למיעבד, אלא אפלוגתא דשאר תנאי בעלמא קאי, דפליגי בעלמא בשאר מילי, כגון אלו מחלוקת דבית שמאי ובית הלל, כלומר כי היכי דפליגי בית שמאי ובית הלל בדברי מחלוקתן:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:2:1.english: And if you wish, say - One who wishes to say that the Mishna teaches [this] did not use Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel specifically; of necessity [the case] is as Beit Hillel wanted to act. Rather, it stands for the dispute of other Tannaim in general, who disagree about other matters in general, such as this dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel; i.e., just as Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree over the matters of their dispute.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:3:1.hebrew: מכל מקום - ברייתא (לא) מתרצה, וקשיא לנהרדעי דעבוד כתרי חומרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:3:1.english: In any case - the baraita is (not) resolved, and it is difficult for the Nehardeans, who act in accordance with two stringencies:

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:4:1.english: Halakha - Like the first Tanna (the anonymous opinion in the Mishnah).

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:4:2.english: And we do not rule so - Rather, [we rule] like Chananiah, who requires doors.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:6:1.hebrew: דסתרן אהדדי - תרי תנאי דפליגי, מר מחמיר ומר מיקל, וטעמא דחומריה דמר בהאי הוי קולא בדוכתא אחריתי, וטעמא דקוליה דמר בהאי הוי חומרא בדוכתא אחריתי, מאן דעבד בהנך תרי דוכתי לחומרא מיקרי כסיל, דהא חד טעמא הוא דהכא הוי חומרא והכא הוי קולא, ואי ההוא טעמא סבירא ליה ליעביד כקוליה וכחומריה:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:6:1.english: That they contradict one another - Two tannaim who disagree, one authority is stringent and one is lenient. The reason for the stringency of the one authority in this case is leniency in another case, and the reason for the leniency of the other authority in this case is stringency in another case. One who follows stringency in both those cases is called a fool, since it is one reason that yields stringency here and leniency there. If he holds that reason, he should act in accordance with its leniency and its stringency.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:7:1.english: Such as a spine and a skull - Of a corpse, about which they disagreed: according to Beit Shammai, it is a lack only when two vertebrae are missing, and if one vertebra is missing it still imparts impurity by overshadowing (ohel). Regarding a terefah as well, it is not a lack and the animal is fit. The reasoning of Beit Shammai is a stringency with regard to a corpse, while Beit Hillel, who say it is a lack, are stringent with regard to a terefah. One who follows Beit Hillel regarding a terefah and Beit Shammai regarding a corpse is a fool, since their rulings contradict each other: here it is a lack, and there it is not a lack.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:7:2.english: The spine and the skull - Regarding the impurity of a tent over a corpse, [in the Mishnah] we learned: How much of a deficiency in the spine would cause it to cease to be a spine and be treated like any other bone? [Namely,] a bone the size of a barley grain, which does not convey impurity in a tent.

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:7:3.english: As much as a drill - And that it be removed from a living [animal] and die, he explains in Bekhorot, in the third chapter:

Rashi on Eruvin 7a:9:1.hebrew: אבל היכא דלא סתרן חומרי אהדדי - כגון הכא דפליגי בתרי מילי דתליין בתרי טעמא, מר מחמיר בהא עקום, ומר מחמיר בהא מפולש, ולא סתרן חומרי אהדדי עבדינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 7a:9:1.english: But where the stringencies do not contradict each other - Such as here, where they disagree about two matters that depend on two different reasons: one authority is stringent about this one, [a bent alley], and the other is stringent about that one, [an open-through alley], and since the stringencies do not contradict each other, we follow them.

Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:10:1.hebrew: ונהג בו ב' עישורים - מפרש בירושלמי, שעישר על תנאי וחללו, ונתנו לעניים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:10:1.english: And he treated it with two tithes - The Yerushalmi explains that he tithed conditionally, then declared it unconsecrated (ḥullin) and gave it to the poor.

Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:13:1.hebrew: בקעה מכאן ובקעה מכאן מיבעיא - ולא משמע ליה, דאתא לאשמועינן דאפ"ה בעי צורת הפתח, אלא אתי לאשמועינן דסגי בצורת הפתח:
Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:13:1.english: Is it necessary to ask: 'a valley on this side and a valley on that side'? - And it does not seem to him that [the Gemara] came to teach that even in that case one requires a tzurat ha-petach (the form of a doorway); rather, [the Gemara] came to teach that a tzurat ha-petach suffices.

Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:16:1.hebrew: אם היה מבוי כלה לרחבה אינו צריך כו' - פירש רש"י דנפרצה רחבה כנגדו איירי, דאל"כ מאי אשמועינן? דלאשמועינן דאין רחבה אוסרת על המבוי, לא איצטריך, דרחבה לית בה דיורין, כדאמרינן בפ' ב' (ד' כד:) גבי רחבה דהוה בפום נהרא מאן דשרי משום דלית בה דיורין, והלכתא כרבינא לקולא. ועוד, דאין צריך כלום משמע, דקאי אאיסור פילוש דאיירי ביה. לכך נראה דבנפרצה כנגדו איירי, והא דנקט רחבה ולא נקט חצר, משום דבעי למימר אין צריך כלום, אפילו לא עירבו. אבל חצר דאית ביה דיורין אסור עד שיערבו, דסבר נראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים אינו נידון משום לחי ופתח. ובכלה לאמצע רחבה איירי, ולא חשיב ליה כמפולש, משום דביציאתו מן המבוי יש מקום לנטות לכאן ולכאן, ולא אתי למישרי מפולש:
Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:16:1.english: If there is a mavoi kela (an alley that abuts a square), one needs nothing, etc. - Rashi explained that the statement deals with a case where the square has been breached opposite it; otherwise, what would it be teaching us? If it were teaching that a square does not render the alley forbidden, it would be unnecessary, since a square has no residents, as we said in chapter 2 (Eruvin 24b) regarding a square at the mouth of a river, where one who permits it does so because it has no residents, and the halakha follows Ravina's leniency. Furthermore, 'one needs nothing' implies that it refers to the prohibition of *mefulash* (an alley open through to the far side), which the Gemara is discussing. Therefore it appears that it deals with a breach opposite it. As for the fact that the statement says 'square' and not 'courtyard', it is because it intends to say 'one needs nothing at all, even if they did not make an eruv.' But a courtyard that has residents is forbidden until they make an eruv, since its author holds that something that appears from outside and is level inside is not judged as *lechi* and *petah* (jamb and doorway). And it deals with an alley that opens into the middle of the square, and it is not considered a *mefulash*, because upon exiting the alley there is room to turn this way or that way, and it does not come to permit a *mefulash*.

Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:7:1.english: Such as a spine and a skull - This implies that the ruling “likewise for a trefah” applies to both of them. And if you ask, what do Beit Hillel mean? [Their point is] that it is removed from the living and dies; but Beit Shammai too [hold that it] dies at their measure. And furthermore, what does Rav Yehudah teach us, who said, “Likewise for a trefah regarding the skull, since it dies from it”? One can answer that it is more common to die through removal with a minor defect than through decay and illness. And if you ask about these trefot (Chullin 42b), where the Gemara asks, “But there are [trefot] of S.G.R., Shav Shema'ata, and Samekh, which are a defect in the spine, so why does it not also ask about the skull?” One can answer that a defect of the skull renders an animal trefah because the end of the membrane of the brain would be severed, and it is included among the eighteen trefot. But a defect of the spine does not, because the end of the cord would be severed; the Gemara speaks even [of a case] below the parashot, where severing the cord does not render it trefah.

Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:7:2.hebrew: (ומיהו כמה בני אדם שניטל הרבה מעצם גולגלתם ולא ניקב הקרום וחיו, וצ"ל דחסרון הגולגולת הוי עם קרום העליון, ואע"ג דאיכא למ"ד דבבהמה בכה"ג בנקיבת קרום העליון טריפה, היינו משום דסוף התחתון ליפסק; אבל באדם אין סופו ליפסק, לפי שהוא קשה וחזק באדם יותר מבהמה, ולכך צריך חסרון העצם; אבל למ"ד עד דאינקיב תתאה, אדם ובהמה שוים, דבין באדם בין בבהמה כי נפסק העצם עם הקרום, סוף התחתון ליפסק):
Tosafot on Eruvin 7a:7:2.english: However, there are several people from whom much of the bone of the skull was removed without the membrane being pierced, and they lived. It must be said that the defect of the skull is to be understood together with the upper membrane. Even though there is one opinion that in an animal, in such a case where the upper membrane is pierced, it is terefah, that is only because the lower [membrane] will eventually be severed. But in a human, it will not eventually be severed, since it is harder and stronger in a human than in an animal; therefore the loss of the bone is required. But according to the one who holds that [it is terefah only] once the lower [membrane] is pierced, a human and an animal are equal, for whether in a human or in an animal, when the bone is severed together with the membrane, the lower [membrane] will eventually be severed.
